hook: If you leave conversations replaying everything you said — you're not anxious. You're doing something specific with your attention that's making it worse.
body:
**If you leave a conversation and immediately start replaying it — picking apart what you said, what you should have said, how you came across — that's not just anxiety. That's your attention going in the wrong direction.**

During the conversation, your attention was split. Part of you was in the room, and part of you was watching yourself be in the room. And that inner observer isn't kind. It's not watching with curiosity. It's watching with a checklist.

What that split attention costs you is the thing people actually feel as charisma: presence.

When you're truly present with someone — when your full attention is on them, not on how you're performing — they feel it. Not because you said anything brilliant. Because you were actually there.

The people you find most magnetic aren't doing anything complicated. They're just not watching themselves while they're talking to you. All their attention is pointed outward, toward you, and that attention feels like being seen.

The post-conversation replay is your nervous system trying to catch what it missed. What it missed is that the other person was there to connect, not to evaluate you.

The guide in my bio goes deeper on this — link is there.
